/-!
# Cycle double cover conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cycle double cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/cycle_double_cover_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz73] Szekeres, G., *Polyhedral decompositions of cubic graphs*,
  Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 8 (1973), 367--387.
- [Se79] Seymour, P. D., *Sums of circuits*, in Graph Theory and Related Topics (1979), 341--355.

A *cycle double cover* of a graph is a collection of cycles that together include each edge of
the graph exactly twice. The **cycle double cover conjecture** states that every bridgeless graph
has a cycle double cover.

Here a *cycle* is a connected subgraph all of whose vertices have degree two, so a single edge
traversed back and forth is not a cycle. Cycle graphs and bridgeless cactus graphs only have
double covers that use the same cycle twice, so the collection is a *multiset* of cycles and
edges are counted with multiplicity.

The conjecture is stated for finite simple graphs. This loses no generality: subdividing every
edge of a bridgeless multigraph gives a bridgeless simple graph, and a cycle double cover of the
subdivision contracts to one of the original multigraph.
-/

theorem not_isCycleDoubleCover_of_isBridge {G : SimpleGraph V} {e : Sym2 V} (he : G.IsBridge e)
    (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : ¬ IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  intro hC
  obtain ⟨hmem, hcyc⟩ := isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem.mp he
  have h2 := hC e hmem
  have h0 : C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 0 :=
    Multiset.countP_eq_zero.mpr fun c _ => hcyc c.walk c.isCycle
  omega

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop: for every finite undirected bridgeless graph (formalizable over `SimpleGraph` with `Fintype V`, using `SimpleGraph.IsBridgeless` and `SimpleGraph.Cycle` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib; the article's reduction shows the simple-graph case suffices since subdividing edges preserves bridgelessness), there exists a *multiset* of cycles (duplicates allowed, e.g. cycle graphs need the same cycle twice) where each cycle is a genuine simple cycle (connected, 2-regular; a single edge back-and-forth does not count) and every edge lies in *exactly* two members counted with multiplicity; the edgeless/empty graph is bridgeless and satisfied by the empty multiset, and the article's 'July 2026 proof' section contradicts the recorded open status and is irrelevant to the question posed.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition (finite SimpleGraph, IsBridgeless, Multiset (Cycle G), each edge in exactly two members counted with multiplicity); differences are only cosmetic (filter.card vs countP, edgeSet vs edgeFinset, bespoke predicate or inline). c08 chosen as base for the most complete module docstring (references Sz73/Se79 matching citations.jsonl, explicit note on the multigraph-to-simple reduction and on multiset semantics), plus proved test/API lemmas (edgeless graph bridgeless, empty multiset covers ⊥, a bridge blocks any cover). I added c03's concrete triangle test (two copies of the unique cycle double cover K3), which exercises the multiset semantics that the article stresses. Final file compiles with only the sorry warning.

context:
In graph-theoretic mathematics, a cycle double cover is a collection of cycles in an undirected graph that together include each edge of the graph exactly twice. For instance, for any polyhedral graph, the faces of a convex polyhedron that represents the graph provide a cycle double cover of the graph: the edges of each face form a cycle and each edge belongs to exactly two faces and therefore to two of these cycles.
It is a problem posed in the 1970s by W. T. Tutte, Itai and Rodeh, George Szekeres and Paul Seymour and known as the cycle double cover conjecture, whether every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover. The conjecture can equivalently be formulated in terms of graph embeddings, and in that context is also known as the circular embedding conjecture.
In July 2026, OpenAI released a preprint claiming a positive resolution of the conjecture, the proof of which they claim was generated by GPT-5.6, its large language model.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (multiset, exactly two, genuine simple cycles, finite simple graphs suffice, edgeless case, ignore the 'proposed solution' section) all match the article and were followed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cycle double cover conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cycle double cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/cycle_double_cover_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz73] Szekeres, G., *Polyhedral decompositions of cubic graphs*,
  Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 8 (1973), 367--387.
- [Se79] Seymour, P. D., *Sums of circuits*, in Graph Theory and Related Topics (1979), 341--355.

A *cycle double cover* of a graph is a collection of cycles that together include each edge of
the graph exactly twice. The **cycle double cover conjecture** states that every bridgeless graph
has a cycle double cover.

Here a *cycle* is a connected subgraph all of whose vertices have degree two, so a single edge
traversed back and forth is not a cycle. Cycle graphs and bridgeless cactus graphs only have
double covers that use the same cycle twice, so the collection is a *multiset* of cycles and
edges are counted with multiplicity.

The conjecture is stated for finite simple graphs. This loses no generality: subdividing every
edge of a bridgeless multigraph gives a bridgeless simple graph, and a cycle double cover of the
subdivision contracts to one of the original multigraph.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- A multiset `C` of cycles of `G` is a *cycle double cover* of `G` if every edge of `G` lies in
exactly two members of `C`, counted with multiplicity. -/
def IsCycleDoubleCover (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 2

/--
**Cycle double cover conjecture** (Szekeres 1973, Seymour 1979).
Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that includes each edge twice.
Precisely: for every finite bridgeless undirected graph $G$ there is a multiset of cycles
of $G$ such that every edge of $G$ belongs to exactly two members of the multiset, counted with
multiplicity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle G), IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  sorry

omit [DecidableEq V] in
/-- The graph with no edges is bridgeless. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isBridgeless_bot : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).IsBridgeless := by
  intro e he
  simp at he

/-- The empty multiset is a cycle double cover of the graph with no edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_bot_zero : IsCycleDoubleCover (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) 0 := by
  intro e he
  simp at he

/-- The triangle `0 → 1 → 2 → 0` as a cycle of the complete graph on three vertices. -/
def triangleCycle : Cycle (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) where
  base := 0
  walk := .cons (u := 0) (v := 1) (by decide) (.cons (u := 1) (v := 2) (by decide)
    (.cons (u := 2) (v := 0) (by decide) .nil))
  isCycle := by
    rw [Walk.isCycle_def, Walk.isTrail_def]
    exact ⟨by decide, by simp, by decide⟩

/-- The triangle is double covered by two copies of its only cycle. This shows why the cover is a
multiset rather than a set. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_top_fin_three :
    IsCycleDoubleCover (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) {triangleCycle, triangleCycle} := by
  intro e he
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h a b =>
    simp only [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all <;> decide

/-- A cycle double cover of a graph with an edge is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleDoubleCover.ne_zero {G : SimpleGraph V} {C : Multiset (Cycle G)}
    (hC : IsCycleDoubleCover G C) {e : Sym2 V} (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) : C ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  simpa using hC e he

/-- A bridge lies on no cycle, so a graph with a bridge has no cycle double cover. This is why
the conjecture assumes that the graph is bridgeless. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isCycleDoubleCover_of_isBridge {G : SimpleGraph V} {e : Sym2 V} (he : G.IsBridge e)
    (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : ¬ IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  intro hC
  obtain ⟨hmem, hcyc⟩ := isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem.mp he
  have h2 := hC e hmem
  have h0 : C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 0 :=
    Multiset.countP_eq_zero.mpr fun c _ => hcyc c.walk c.isCycle
  omega

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

items: The list entry says 'includes each edge twice'; following the article ('exactly twice', 'precisely two elements of the multiset') this is formalized as exactly 2, via Multiset.countP = 2.

'Family of cycles' is modeled as a Multiset (Cycle G), as the article explicitly says a multiset is needed (cycle graphs need the same cycle twice). Each Cycle G is a trail, so each member contributes at most 1 to the count of an edge.

Graphs are finite simple graphs (SimpleGraph V with Fintype V), per the decomposition table. The conjecture is usually stated for multigraphs; the simple-graph case is equivalent by subdividing edges (bridgelessness is preserved and covers pull back), as recorded in the module docstring.

SimpleGraph.Cycle bundles a basepoint, so the same geometric cycle has several representatives (rotations/reversals). Counting them as separate members is harmless: it is the same as using a cycle with multiplicity, which the statement permits.

Bridgeless uses the repo's SimpleGraph.IsBridgeless (∀ e ∈ edgeSet, ¬ IsBridge e), where Mathlib's IsBridge means the edge's endpoints become unreachable after deleting it — equivalent to 'removal increases the number of components'. The hypothesis is genuinely restrictive (a bridge blocks any cover; proved as an API lemma).
[DecidableEq V] is assumed so that membership e ∈ c.edges is decidable for countP; this is the same convention as the existing Alon–Tarsi file and does not change the mathematical content.
Edgeless graphs (including empty V) are bridgeless and satisfied by the empty multiset; tested with isBridgeless_bot and isCycleDoubleCover_bot_zero.
The article's 'July 2026 proposed solution' section is ignored; the category is `research open` as recorded in the task status.

reviewer_notes: Verification: SimpleGraph.Cycle bundles Walk.IsCycle, giving edges.Nodup (each member counts an edge at most once) and 3 ≤ length (back-and-forth edge excluded). IsBridgeless = ∀ e ∈ edgeSet, ¬ IsBridge e (Mathlib IsBridge: endpoints unreachable after deletion). 'Includes each edge twice' read as exactly two, per the article's formulation section. Empty vertex type / edgeless graphs are bridgeless and covered by the empty multiset (vacuous edge quantifier) — matches the decomposition notes. DecidableEq V is only for countP decidability; the truth value is independent of the instance. Finite simple graphs per the decomposition; the reduction from multigraphs by edge subdivision is valid and recorded in the module docstring. Bundled basepoints mean a geometric cycle has multiple Cycle G representatives, but this does not affect existence of a double cover. The article's future-dated 'July 2026 proposed solution' section was ignored; category is research open per the recorded status. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised, and I found none warranted.
